enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
518 PM MDT Sat Oct 17 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 517 PM MDT Sat Oct 17 2026

 - Gradually increasing rain chances Sunday afternoon into Tuesday.

 - Much better areawide rain chances Wednesday and Thursday with 
   chances for flooding potential and strong storms.

 - Cool today, but increasing warmth the next few days with highs
   in the upper 70s and low 80s again by Tuesday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1137 AM MDT Sat Oct 17 2026

Cutoff low will continue to spin over Baja California and SoCal 
today, trying to push in some moisture from the southwest but expect 
dry conditions today. Pressure gradient is still pretty tight along 
and west of the Continental Divide leading to some breezy conditions 
this afternoon. Still keeping an eye out for dust on the Lordsburg 
Playa but the cooler air will help keep it down but breezy winds 
could create some dust. This closed low gets picked up and starts 
progressing the trough towards our area Sunday. Low end showery 
activity possible Sunday afternoon for western NM. A shortwave is 
what will be left of the upper low but looks to provide enough 
energy and moisture to bring some showery activity overnight into 
Monday morning mostly focusing west of the Rio Grande Valley 
(RGV). PWs Monday and Tuesday will be well above average 
(0.8"-0.9") but instability parameters don't look very impressive 
(~200-500 J/kg). 

Another upper low slides south off the west coast of the CONUS from 
the Gulf of Alaska. By Wednesday, this closed low is off the coast 
of SoCal while there's a ridge just to our southeast. As time goes 
on, expect this low to inch closer to make landfall near SoCal 
before lifting out to the northeast. This will allow for
anomalously high moisture (PWs of an 1" Wednesday, increasing to 
1.1"-1.3" Thursday) to push in. For reference, the average PW for 
middle of Oct is 0.5", 90th percentile is 0.8". and maximum values
upwards of 1.15". Wednesday and Thursday have the potential to 
become quite active with this upper trough. Instability values do 
look better during this time, in addition to 0-6km shear values of
anywhere from 20-50kt. Better shear looks to be focused out west 
during this time. There will be a risk for flash flooding with 
thunderstorms, as well as some strong thunderstorms. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAFS)
Issued at 517 PM MDT Sat Oct 17 2026

VFR conditions through the period with SCT080 SCT-BKN250. After
17Z west of Deming...isolated BKN060 -SHRA. Winds southeast
8-12knots, except 10-15G25 knots over Hidalgo and southern Grant
Counties. Winds diminishing all areas after 03Z east 7-10 knots. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 121 PM MDT Sat Oct 17 2026

Increasing moisture tomorrow will increase min RHs to 35-40% across 
the lowlands and 45-50% in the mountains Sunday. Expect similar min 
RHs through much of next weeK with 20 foot winds staying light each 
afternoon at 5-10 mph. Low end chances for showers and storms Sunday 
afternoon through Tuesday with a focus being over western areas 
bordering AZ. Anomalously moist air pushes in Wednesday and 
Thursday which may bring a risk of flash flooding and strong 
thunderstorms. Temperatures warm each day Sunday through Thursday.
Temperatures will stay below normal for this time of year Sunday 
and Monday becoming near seasonal to above average mid-week.
